title: Applied ML experiment scratchpad - quant + eval notes (2026-03-31)
content:
Date: 2026-03-31
Owner: Asha Kapoor (applied-ml)
Context: quick personal scratchpad for the ongoing quantization vs 8-bit eval runs. Trying to capture experimental configs, early metrics, and short TODOs so I can hand off to Jordan/Samira if needed.

Goal:
- Compare GPTQ-style 4-bit (q4_0 / q4_k_m) vs 8-bit (nf4/fp8-ish) on our internal QA + summarization evals. Measure latency/throughput, macro QA accuracy (exact match/F1), and obvious hallucination/regression signals.

Datasets:
- qa-eval-2026-03 (200 prompts, mixed-domain: KB, how-to, math)
- summarization-dev-100 (long docs ~800 tokens)

Experiment matrix (high level):
- Model baseline: redwood/vicuna-13b-v1 (fp16 baseline)
- Quant variants: q4_gptq_perchannel, q4_k_m, nf4_8bit, int8-fp32-mix
- KV-cache: enabled / disabled (impact on serving latency for streaming)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8 (simulate low-latency vs batched throughput)
- Temp: 0.0 for QA; 0.2 for summarization

Runs (notes on runs I launched today):
- run: q4_gptq_run_2026-03-31_A
  - model: vicuna-13b-v1
  - quant: q4_gptq_perchannel (calibrated w/ 512 steps)
  - kv-cache: enabled
  - batch: 4
  - dataset: qa-eval-2026-03
  - config id: cfg-q4-a
  - prelim metrics: latency p95=210ms, throughput=95 tokens/s, QA EM=73.9%
  - notes: occasional tokenization edge-case on math prompts (investigate tokenizer mismatch)

- run: int8_run_2026-03-31_B
  - quant: nf4-ish 8-bit (simulated on CPU emu)
  - kv-cache: enabled
  - batch: 4
  - prelim metrics: latency p95=280ms, throughput=70 tokens/s, QA EM=75.8%
  - notes: higher quality but much slower on our current kernel selection (need to re-evaluate kernel mapping)

- run: q4_km_run_2026-03-31_C (quick ablation)
  - quant: q4_k_m (kmeans approx)
  - kv-cache: disabled (to check perf without KV)
  - batch: 1
  - prelim metrics: latency p95=150ms, throughput=120 tokens/s, QA EM=72.2%
  - notes: disabling kv-cache reduced p95 but increased token compute; weird that throughput improved for small batch (check batching codepath)

Preliminary observations:
- 4-bit GPTQ gets us close to 8-bit accuracy within ~2-3% EM on QA but with noticeably better throughput on our serving kernels.
- 8-bit routes currently map to slower kernels (need to check kernel selection heuristics in runtime). Potential to tune compilation to favor int8 kernels for certain seq lengths.
- KV-cache interactions are non-linear: disabling cache reduces p95 on single-request runs (no cache-warmup overhead) but hurts throughput for longer sessions. Need a systematic microbenchmark.
- Some hallucination cases surfaced on long-context summarization for q4 variants — likely numerical/precision-sensitive tokens. Flagging these prompts for eval set.

Quick checklist / TODO (priority order):
- [ ] Re-run q4_gptq with explicit tokenizer alignment (ensure same vocab/truncation as baseline) (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Create microbench harness: 1-token incremental generation p50/p95 for each quant config (owner: Jordan)
- [ ] Add summarization long-context eval (owner: Samira)
- [ ] Open perf issue: kernel selection favors slow int8 kernel on A100-like hardware (JIRA-4567) (owner: Asha)
- [ ] Try fused-kv-cache + q4 pipeline (owner: Jordan/Samira)
- [ ] Add automatic regression alert: notify if EM drops >5% vs baseline on primary QA set

Calibration / prompt notes:
- Need to add 10 calibration prompts (edge-case numeric, code blocks) when running GPTQ calibration; current calibration set too web-text heavy.
- Prompt template used for QA: "Q: <context>
Question: <q>
A:" (keeps answers short) — ensure stop tokens consistent across runs.

Quick commands/links (for my later recall):
- local run (small): ./scripts/eval_run.sh --model vicuna-13b-v1 --quant q4_gptq --batch 4 --dataset qa-eval-2026-03
- perf trace: gh pr 2345 (runtime kernel mapping changes)
- confluence: https://confluence.redwood/applied-ml/quant-eval

Notes to self:
- If q4_gptq holds ~within 2% quality and gives 25-40% throughput improvement, plan to push as default for non-sensitive workloads + add opt-out flag for customers.
- For Dedicated customers, need explicit notes about reproducibility and binary artifacts (packaged GPTQ scales).

Hand-off summary (if I have to step out):
- Jordan: run microbench harness + try fused-kv + q4 test (see TODO)
- Samira: add summarization long-context tests + sample hallucination cases into the eval dashboard

End of scratchpad. Will tidy into a PR / confluence summary once we have stable numbers.
